# Symmetry, grammars and cellular automata {#sec-symmetry}

## Symmetry groups

Repeating plane patterns fall into the 7 frieze groups (one direction of
translation, i.e. *bands*) and the 17 wallpaper groups (two directions)
[@grunbaum1987tilings; overviews in @wiki_frieze and @wiki_wallpaper]. @washburn1988symmetries made symmetry
classification a standard tool for analysing textile and ceramic design
across cultures. @liu2004computational give an algorithm that detects the
frieze or wallpaper group of a periodic image, which could be used on the
Sjónabók bands directly.

For generation this suggests a cheap and powerful split: generate only a
**fundamental region** and produce the rest by applying the group. A
rosette with dihedral symmetry $D_4$ needs one eighth of the square; a
border with a horizontal mirror needs half a period. Almost all hard
"structure" problems (balance, symmetry, period) then disappear by
construction, and a texture method (@sec-wfc, @sec-texture) only has to
fill a small region. Symmetry in the corpus is measured in
@sec-corpus.

## Shape grammars and L-systems

Shape grammars [@stiny1972shape] generate designs by rewriting labelled
shapes, and have been used to model historical ornament styles.
L-systems [@prusinkiewicz1990algorithmic] rewrite strings that are
interpreted as drawing commands and are well suited to branching,
vine-like borders. Both are deterministic given a seed and rule weights,
and both give explicit control of large-scale structure, but writing a
grammar that captures a style is manual work.

## Cellular automata

Elementary cellular automata [@wolfram1983statistical; @wolfram2002new; @wiki_eca]
produce rich binary patterns row by row, which matches the row-by-row nature
of knitting. They are an interesting source of novel texture but they do not
learn from examples, so "in the vein of Sjónabók" would have to be achieved
by searching for rules whose output scores well against the corpus
(@sec-evaluation).

## Fit for this project

Symmetry-group generation is the strongest candidate for the *structure*
layer of a hybrid: it is trivial to implement, fully reproducible, and
directly reflects how the corpus is built. Grammars are a possible later
layer for banner composition. Cellular automata are a curiosity here.
